source.title: Find the Number of Copy Arrays

teaching.hint: How many independent choices remain once all consecutive differences have been fixed?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Equal consecutive differences force copy-original to be one constant shift; every bound restricts that same integer.
solution_outline.approach: Translate each index’s value bounds into an interval for the common shift. Intersect all those intervals, then count their inclusive integer points, returning zero for an empty intersection.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The running lower and upper limits describe exactly the shifts satisfying all processed indices.
solution_outline.correctness: Subtracting the difference equations makes copy[i]-original[i] equal to its predecessor, hence constant. Conversely every constant shift preserves all differences. Its per-index bounds are exactly the translated intervals, so the common shifts in their intersection are in bijection with valid arrays.
solution_outline.pitfall: An empty intersection gives zero, not a negative inclusive interval length.

source_fidelity_notes: Retained equality of every adjacent difference, per-index inclusive bounds, and integer-array counting; omitted enumerated examples.
common_wrong_turns: An empty intersection gives zero, not a negative inclusive interval length.
